headline: The UK Law Commission has proposed updating product liability law so that software and AI systems count as products.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score; an official proposal on a major legal question, but it is only a consultation.
importance_line: It could eventually let people harmed by defective software or AI claim compensation and raise the liability risk for developers, but these are proposals for consultation, with final recommendations not expected before late 2027 and any change needing legislation.
summary: Legal IT Insider reports that the UK Law Commission, which advises on law reform, opened a consultation on 8 Oct 2026 on updating product liability law, which dates from almost 40 years ago and covers only physical goods. The proposals would extend the definition of "product" to software, AI systems and online platforms and give consumers clearer rights to compensation when a product is defective; the consultation closes on 14 Jan 2027, with final recommendations expected in late 2027.
notes: Consultation proposals, not law. Article does not say whether the proposals cover England and Wales only or the whole UK; 'any change needing legislation' is a general legal point, not in the article.
